body.heading: Make the fishing rod
paragraphs: Your adult ties a large magnet firmly to a string and a stick. Decorate card fish and slide a paper clip onto each one.
Scatter the fish on the floor. Now dangle the magnet over them and fish. The magnet pulls the paper clips without even touching them.

body.heading: An invisible pull
paragraphs: Magnets pull some metals — iron and steel — with an invisible force. The force works through card, through water, and even through your hand.
Not everything metal is magnetic. Many coins and foil usually ignore the magnet completely. Test and see.

body.heading: Sort the catch
paragraphs: Make two piles: things the magnet caught, and things it ignored. Your piles are a science result.
Fridge doors, catches, and some toys all hide magnets. Once you start fishing, you find magnets everywhere.

takeaway: Magnets pull iron and steel with an invisible force, and a fishing game shows which things answer the pull.
materials: A large magnet tied to string on a stick (an adult prepares)
safetyNotes: Magnets must stay away from mouths — swallowing a magnet is dangerous, so an adult holds the fishing rod at all times and counts the magnets before and after. Keep magnets away from phones and bank cards.
screenFreeExtension: Test ten more objects around one room and keep a magnetic-or-not score chart.
